independently_inspected_facts.fact: The five scoped areas are existing descendants of the baseline parent hierarchy. Their metadata declares WGSRPD level 3 as basis; TDWG says WGSRPD is for recording plant distributions, with a Botanical Country level that may ignore purely political factors. UN M49 provides a separate statistical regional/naming scheme. Neither reference alone verifies that the Atlas areas have suitable purpose or boundaries.
independently_inspected_facts.limit: Area membership was exactly reproduced from baseline location→province→area parent links, but the source-purpose fit and boundary correspondence remain unresolved.

known_limits: The geoBoundaries API is a current endpoint, but each metadata response links to the pinned 9469f09 GeoJSON release; hashes and raw response bytes are retained. It is provider metadata, not a cryptographic publisher signature.
DRC issue scope’s exact 169-member subset excludes 20 of the 189 features in the retained country-wide source file; the other packet scopes own separate workloads.
Gabon’s retained source has 49 features, while the Ministry page cites 48 departments in 2016; no count alone resolves the 2018 source roster.
Equatorial Guinea’s issue metadata and geoBoundaries API conflict on canonical role (District vs Unknown). The 2013 source predates Djibloho and 2025–26 changes.

Official/legal raw pages with uncertain or restricted reuse are not retained. For DRC and Gabon the source HTML/PDF raw hash was unavailable because direct fetch timed out or TLS failed; restoration URLs are exact.
Source and identity hashes validate bytes and roster linking only, not territorial meaning, completeness, hierarchy, topology or boundaries.
